(5) prior_art_librarian ('does the repo already import a real HTML tokenizer?'): CHECKED — yes, golang.org/x/net/html (go.mod v0.46.0, indirect), imported by datahelpers/claims.go and actions/section_visible_text.go. Both ask what a document CONTAINS — parse questions on assumed-whole documents, where WHATWG error recovery is exactly right. These guards ask whether a document is CUT, and spec EOF-recovery normalises the malformedness they exist to detect: a tokenizer at EOF inside an open tag emits NO StartTag, so '...<script src="/a.js' (cut mid-open-tag) would PASS tag balance where both the old counter and this scanner flag it; at EOF in script data it simply stops, leaving 'open with no close' to be reconstructed from tokenizer state. Holding the calibration at ZERO verdict flips across all 264 recorded component_versions rows required deciding those EOF edges the old counter's way, which a spec tokenizer deliberately does not. This answer now lives in markup_balance.go's header (commit 0e21e3cf1) so it is not re-litigated. plan.risks: 1) A false NEGATIVE (a real cut passing the new counter) is the failure that matters. Mitigations: browser-faithful raw-text semantics (a mid-JS cut always leaves <script unmatched); 0 verdict flips across all 264 component_versions rows including every recorded casualty; the 60%-cut negative control on real tool templates; EOF edge cases deliberately decided the OLD counter's way (open cut mid-tag still counts; close cut before '>' does not) — the two shapes where a spec tokenizer would have LOST true positives. Residual: a cut inside an HTML comment is invisible to tag balance under BOTH predicates (endsCleanly still catches it on the tool path; the section birth path never caught it either — no regression). 2) The token LIST for templates cut inside a raw-text body is shorter than before (only the enclosing tag; verdict unchanged) — one discovery-test expectation was updated with the reasoning in place. 3) Two open truncated_component items are false alarms: deliberately left open (acting on their remedy text before the roll is the danger — one advises restoring v1 over a GOOD template); their verifier resolves them post-roll; recorded in the bug file, LANDMINES remedy note, and the workstream memory. 4) Go changes inert until an image rolls; the pod-verification recipe with both controls is in the bug file.
